'''Carol Smith Schumacher''' (born 1960){{r|wc}} is a Bolivian-born American mathematician specializing in [[real analysis]], a [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]], and a textbook author. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Kenyon College]], and vice president of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].{{r|kendir}}

==Early life and education==
Schumacher was born in [[La Paz]], [[Bolivia]]{{r|ccbio}} as the daughter of missionaries, and grew up in Bolivia speaking both English and Spanish.{{r|lathisms}} She majored in mathematics at [[Hendrix College]] in [[Conway, Arkansas]], and graduated with honors in 1982.{{r|cv}} It was in freshman calculus at Hendrix that she met her husband, physicist and [[quantum information theory|quantum information theorist]] [[Benjamin Schumacher]].{{r|hendrix}}

She went to the [[University of Texas at Austin]] for graduate study, and completed her Ph.D. in 1989 with a dissertation on the theory of [[Banach space]]s, jointly supervised by [[Edward Odell]] and [[Haskell P. Rosenthal]].{{r|cv|mg}}

==Career and contributions==
Schumacher joined Kenyon College as Dana Assistant Professor in 1988, has been full professor there since 2002,{{r|cv}} and has been department chair for several terms. She was elected vice president of the Mathematical Association of America for the 2018–2020 term.{{r|vpmaa}}

Schumacher is the author of two [[inquiry-based learning]] textbooks:{{r|lathisms}} ''Chapter Zero: Fundamental Notions of Abstract Mathematics'', on the transition to proofs (Addison-Wesley, 1996; 2nd edition, 2001){{r|cz}} and ''Closer and Closer: Introducing Real Analysis'', on [[real analysis]] (Jones and Bartlett, 2008).{{r|cc}}

==Recognition==
Kenyon College gave Schumacher their Senior Trustee Teaching Excellence Award in 2005.{{r|cv|trustee}} She was the 2017 winner of the Distinguished Teaching Award of the Ohio Section of the Mathematical Association of America.{{r|ohio}}

Schumacher is a 2023 recipient of one of the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]].{{r|haimo}}
